models.summary: Three tiers of parameters, individual, family and society, cross three factors, income, education and equality, drawn from the 2015 PUMS file of 1,618,489 people, which has no records under age 16. Disposable income is real income times one minus the tax rate. The saving rate is one minus consumption over disposable income, and its sign is read as distress, comfort or anxiety. Childcare rate is family childcare over family expenditure. Output is productivity times population times one minus unemployment, and net product subtracts the floor times its headcount and the childcare budget. Schooling averages expected years over 15 and mean years over 18. Inequality is the Gini coefficient. Weights come from word frequency in a research database, then an analytic hierarchy process on the 1-9 scale: equality weighs 0.550 in happiness against 0.247 income and 0.202 education, with maximum eigenvalue 3.0044 and consistency ratio 0.0043.

models.summary: Ten thousand founders are filtered, not sampled: innovators, defined as under 40 with a bachelor's degree, outnumber producers 7 to 3, skilled labor outnumbers unskilled 9 to 1, sex is exactly even, and spouses migrate together. Against a random draw of the same size the selected group has income spread 46,844 against 52,044, higher schooling and a younger age mix, while weekly hours barely differ, so that filter is dropped. Each person carries six attributes. Death is logistic in age, centered at 70. Unemployment is fixed at 5 percent, the floor at 5,000, tax at 0.15, retirement at 65, and one year of leave pays 40,000. Income is a normal draw around last year's productivity, scaled by schooling and by distance from age 35. Schooling stops are drawn from last year's distribution. Marriage probability falls with a distance that mixes age gap and income gap, and the closest pair marries first. Couples aged 19 to 40 expect two children over twenty years.

models.summary: The wage floor is searched only near half the average income, not globally. Families fall in five brackets at the floor, 35,000, 60,000, 85,000 and 160,000, with shares 5, 20, 45, 25 and 10 percent, and move by a transition chart whose rates keep those shares fixed. Three objectives maximize average income, minimize the spread and maximize the floor. A controlled elitist genetic algorithm over 50 iterations returns the point (65,234, 9,848, 33,526). Parental leave adds a sixth class paid a flat amount, and the birth probability is an arctangent of that pay centered at 55,000. The spread is minimized at a leave pay of 50,200 per parent, which barely moves average income and lowers the floor only slightly.

models.summary: Happiness splits by age and schooling: the young and the old are slightly happier than the middle-aged, who support both children and parents, and high-school graduates are less happy because they work longer for less. Three subgroups follow. Professionals want time off and parental leave. Unskilled workers want hours, disability care, childcare and the wage floor. The unemployed are named but given no priority. Allocation is cut to two groups and two resources. A nonlinear program minimizes the drop from the previous global outcome plus penalties on unequal shares, so fairness is a cost. The four allocation amounts are the strategy.
models.purpose: Split limited budgets without abandoning the global outcome.

models.summary: A social graph takes people as nodes and every tie except marriage and parenthood as edges, justified by short paths, clustering above random graphs, and a power-law degree distribution. Links form between people of the same occupation and schooling, and when someone is tied to both of another's parents. A high degree is read as wealth and high connectivity as equality. Ten thousand immigrants arrive every ten years with no children under 16, which opens a sixteen-year age gap. Of five arrival years, years 10 and 30 win because they drop a new boom into that gap. Moving 50,000 people as 10,000 every ten years beats moving all 50,000 in year 50, both because the gap closes and because jobs scale with last year's output. One percent noise over 30 runs leaves output near 1.35e8 and population near 5,000 at year 50.
